verses.text: These were the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul son of Kish. They were among the mighty warriors who helped him in battle.
They carried bows and could sling stones or shoot arrows with either hand. They were Saul's relatives from the tribe of Benjamin.
Their leader was Ahiezer, followed by Joash. Both were sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. There were also Jeziel and Pelet sons of Azmaveth, Beracah, and Jehu from Anathoth.
They included Ishmaiah from Gibeon, a mighty warrior and leader among the Thirty, along with Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad from Gederah,
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite,
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam from the Korahites,
and Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

Some men from Gad joined David at his stronghold in the wilderness. They were brave, trained fighters who could handle shield and spear. They had faces like lions and were as quick as gazelles in the mountains.
Ezer was their leader, Obadiah was second, and Eliab was third.
Mishmannah was fourth, and Jeremiah was fifth.
Attai was sixth, and Eliel was seventh.
Johanan was eighth, and Elzabad was ninth.
Jeremiah was tenth, and Machbannai was eleventh.
These men of Gad were army commanders. The least of them was a match for a hundred men, and the greatest for a thousand.
They crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it had flooded its banks, and drove away everyone who lived in the valleys on both sides.
Some people from Benjamin and Judah also came to David at the stronghold.

David went out to meet them and said, “If you've come in peace to help me, I'll join with you wholeheartedly. If you've come to betray me to my enemies when I've done nothing wrong, may the God of our ancestors see it and rebuke you.”

Then the Spirit came on Amasai, the leader of the Thirty, and he said, “We're yours, David. We're on your side, son of Jesse. Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, because your God helps you.” David welcomed them and made them commanders in his force.

Some men from Manasseh joined David when he went with the Philistines to fight Saul. David and his men didn't fight with them, because the Philistine rulers talked it over and sent him away. They said, “He may go back to his master Saul, and it will cost us our heads.”
As David went to Ziklag, men from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, another Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai. They commanded units of a thousand in Manasseh.
They helped David against the raiding party. They were all brave warriors and became commanders in the army.
Day after day men came to help David until he had a great army, like the army of God.
These are the numbers of the troops equipped for battle who came to David at Hebron to hand Saul's kingdom over to him, just as the LORD had said.
From Judah came six thousand eight hundred men equipped for battle with shields and spears.
From Simeon came seven thousand one hundred brave warriors ready for battle.
From Levi came four thousand six hundred.
Jehoiada led Aaron's family, and there were three thousand seven hundred with him.
Zadok was a brave young warrior, and twenty-two commanders came from his family.
From Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, came three thousand. Until then most of them had stayed loyal to Saul's family.
From Ephraim came twenty thousand eight hundred brave warriors, men well known in their families.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh came eighteen thousand men chosen by name to go and make David king.
From Issachar came two hundred leaders who understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do. All their relatives were under their command.
From Zebulun came fifty thousand men ready to take their places in battle with every kind of weapon. They stood together without divided loyalties.
From Naphtali came a thousand commanders and thirty-seven thousand men with shields and spears.
From Dan came twenty-eight thousand six hundred men ready to take their places in battle.
From Asher came forty thousand men fit for the army and ready for battle.
From the other side of the Jordan came a hundred and twenty thousand men from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. They were equipped with every kind of weapon for battle.
All these trained soldiers came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. The rest of Israel was of one mind about making David king too.
They spent three days with David, eating and drinking. Their relatives had provided food for them.

People from nearby and from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. They brought plenty of flour, fig cakes, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep, because there was joy in Israel.
